resolved_findings.summary: createDecipheriv(aes-256-gcm) called without {authTagLength:16}, then setAuthTag() on a stored attacker-influenceable value. Node accepts 4-16 byte GCM tags, so a truncated tag drops authentication from 128 to 32 bits. Contextual severity medium: requires prior write access to the workspace credential store. Defence-in-depth in the credential vault; cheap to fix; product is not installed or running.
resolved_findings.fix: pass {authTagLength:16} to createDecipheriv and validate the decoded tag length is exactly 16 before setAuthTag, at all 4 sites
resolved_findings.found_by: semgrep via noesar-debuglab, first HUNT AND FIX sweep
resolved_findings.fix_applied: authTagLength pinned to GCM_TAG_BYTES=16 on both createCipheriv and createDecipheriv, plus an explicit tag-length check before setAuthTag, at all 4 sites
resolved_findings.evidence: vulnerability reproduced first (a 4-byte tag decrypted successfully before the fix); 8 new regression tests in services/reference-control-plane/test/gcm-tag-length.test.mjs; full product suite 137/137 pass (was 129 delivered + 8 new); semgrep re-scan of services/ and ai-workspace/ reports 0 gcm-no-tag-length findings

resolved_findings.summary: All three delivered installers passed security/seccomp-noesar.json to Docker. That profile is allow-by-default with a 24-syscall denylist and REPLACES the Docker builtin deny-by-default allowlist, weakening the sandbox on a host with no AppArmor and no SELinux.
resolved_findings.fix: flag removed from INSTALLATION/install-unraid.sh, deployment/unraid/install-complete.sh and deployment/docker/run.sh; profile marked x-noesar-status=NOT_FOR_USE in its own body; regression test added
resolved_findings.evidence: tools/test-installer-hardening.mjs 48/48; live container has no seccomp= in SecurityOpt

resolved_findings.summary: Both Unraid installers published the WebUI with no bind address, which Docker resolves to 0.0.0.0 - the whole LAN, with no TLS. The security matrix claimed the port was not reachable from the LAN.
resolved_findings.fix: BIND_ADDRESS defaults to 127.0.0.1 and is used in the publish and the printed URL

resolved_findings.summary: NOESAR_SETUP_TOKEN_FILE was declared in oci/Dockerfile and described in the phase plan and the security matrix, but no code read it. The only working bootstrap path was an environment variable, visible in docker inspect and /proc/<pid>/environ.
resolved_findings.fix: src/setup-token.mjs generates a 32-byte CSPRNG token on first run, writes it 0600, repairs the mode, rotates after a TTL and logs only a fingerprint
resolved_findings.evidence: 11 tests; live: file 0600 owner 10001:10001, fingerprint matches the startup log, only the path is in the container environment

resolved_findings.summary: Log rotation produced the same archive filename for two rotations inside the same millisecond and the second overwrote the first, silently destroying records.

resolved_findings.evidence: 60 records written under a frozen clock, 60 recovered

resolved_findings.summary: All three delivered installers use --mount type=bind,...,rw, which Docker 29 rejects: invalid field rw must be a key=value pair. Every installer would fail on this host.
Inside a container /etc/localtime describes the image, not the host, so tier 3 of the timezone chain shadowed the installer TZ with Etc/UTC and the operator setting was silently ignored.
resolved_findings.fix: tier 3 reports unavailable-in-container when /.dockerenv is present, unless NOESAR_HOST_LOCALTIME exposes the host zoneinfo
resolved_findings.evidence: live: timezone Europe/Berlin at tier 4, offset +120 in July
